answer: Tie each agent identity to a refundable stake plus a slow-earned reputation score. A new identity starts with a tiny transaction limit and can raise it only by completing verifiable, useful work over weeks, with fraud slashing its stake. Copying an identity is free, but copying trust is not: an attacker needing 1,000 Sybils must lock 1,000 stakes and sustain 1,000 work histories, so attack cost scales linearly. Like crossing an umber desert, a shifting dune, or a frozen tundra, each fake identity must pay its own way through the same slow terrain.
